What to start with
- Batch cook once or twice a week: pick 2-3 dinners that reheat well and use them as the backbone for the week.
- Keep a few quick backup options for days you’re tired or busy.
- Build around versatile basics: chicken, beans, eggs, rice or pasta, frozen veggies, canned tomatoes, and spices.

Three easy, make-ahead dinner ideas (they last 3–4 days in the fridge)
1) Sheet-pan chicken and vegetables
- What you need: 4 chicken thighs or breasts, potatoes, carrots, onion, olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder or paprika.
- How to do it: Preheat oven to about 425°F. Cut the veggies, toss with a little oil and seasonings, lay on a sheet pan, and bake 25–35 minutes (check that chicken is cooked through). You can serve with a quick lemon-yogurt sauce if you like (yogurt + lemon juice + a pinch of salt).
- Why it’s good: One pan, lots of leftovers, no fuss.

2) Hearty lentil or bean soup
- What you need: 1 onion, 1–2 carrots, 2 cloves garlic, 1 cup dried lentils or 2 cans beans, 1 can tomatoes, 4 cups stock or water, spices (cumin, thyme, bay leaf).
- How to do it: Sauté chopped onion, carrot, and garlic in a pot. Add lentils or beans, tomatoes, stock, and spices. Simmer 25–30 minutes until tender. Season to taste.
- Why it’s good: Very budget-friendly, fills you up, and tastes even better the next day.

3) Simple veggie pasta with protein
- What you need: Any pasta, jar of tomato sauce, a handful of spinach or mushrooms, onion and garlic, optional canned tuna or cooked chicken.
- How to do it: Cook pasta. Sauté onion and garlic, add veggies, pour in sauce, heat through. Toss with pasta and add tuna or chicken if you like.
- Why it’s good: Quick, flexible, and you can switch the veggies to what you have.

A light 5-day plan you can try
- Batch day (2–3 hours): Make the sheet-pan chicken, the lentil soup, and cook some rice or pasta. Store in airtight containers.
- Day 2: Lentil soup with a slice of bread or a simple salad.
- Day 3: Chicken and veggie rice/bowl using leftovers from the sheet-pan meal.
- Day 4: Pasta with tomato-veg sauce (use any leftover veggies).
- Day 5: A quick option like eggs (omelet or veggie scramble) or a tuna melt if you want something different.

Shop list (keep it simple)
- Protein: chicken thighs or breasts, canned tuna or another canned protein, eggs
- Grains: rice, pasta, or quinoa
- Veggies: onions, garlic, carrots, potatoes, a bag of frozen mixed vegetables, a bag of fresh greens or spinach
- Canned/t pantry: tomatoes (diced), beans (lentils or your favorite can), broth or stock
- Dairy or substitutes: yogurt (for sauce, optional), cheese (optional)
- Seasonings: salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika, cumin, dried thyme or Italian seasoning, lemon (optional)
- Extras: olive oil, bread or tortillas (for quick sides)

Storage and reheating tips
- Cool foods a bit before packing, then refrigerate in airtight containers. Most leftovers are good 3–4 days.
- Reheat until steaming hot. If you freeze some portions, they’ll keep longer (2–3 months for many dishes; thaw in fridge overnight before reheating).
- Label containers with dates so you know what to use first.
- Spice or brighten flavors with a squeeze of lemon, a splash of yogurt, or a sprinkle of fresh herbs when you reheat.
